transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Jamal (Redwood) / Priya, Daniel, Hannah, Omar (Lucidity)

Summary: Quick security intake to understand whether Lucidity can use Redwood hosted or needs Dedicated / Private. Main concerns: SSO integration (Okta SAML), KMS / envelope encryption (bring-your-own-key), RBAC mapping to internal roles, audit log retention and chain of custody, and data retention/PII handling.

Topics: SOC2 & ISO posture, SSO/SAML flow, KMS BYOK options, RBAC & least-privilege, audit logs retention/forensics, hosting tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. we also have Liam and Jamal from the solutions team. can folks introduce briefly?
00:12 Priya (Lucidity - CISO): Hi i'm Priya, CISO at Lucidity. i'll lead security gating. we also have Daniel and Hannah on the line.
00:18 Daniel (Lucidity): Daniel here, head of platform, mostly concerned about ops and throughput.
00:22 Hannah (Lucidity): Hannah, devops, i'll handle the infra details.
:27 Maya: Awesome. agenda: SOC2/ISO questions, SSO SAML integration, KMS / encryption, RBAC, audit logs and retention. then decide next steps. anything to add?
00:35 Priya: No that's perfect. main constraint - we are regulated healthcare, so any PHI touching LLMs has to either be private deployment or very strict contractual controls.
00:48 Maya: Totally understood. can you share your timeline and what 'success' looks like for this project?
00:53 Priya: timeline: procurement decision in 6-8 weeks. success = architecture that meets HIPAA‑like controls, SOC2 + ISO evidence, SSO integration, and clear KMS ownership model. also minimal risk around logs holding PHI.
01:08 Daniel: To add, we need predictable latency for UI workflows; if we go hosted, we need SLOs. If dedicated, we want autoscale behavior. cost is a factor but security gates are hard requirement.
01:25 Liam (Redwood SE): quick interjection — to frame options: hosted (fastest to start, we manage keys unless BYOK configured), dedicated (reserved GPU pool, more isolation, ability to control network egress), private/VPC (customer-run control plane or on-prem, full KMS control with HSM integrations).
01:44 Hannah: When you say BYOK, do you mean we can bring our AWS KMS key and you never see plaintext? how does the envelope flow work?
01:51 Jamal: Good question. short answer: we support envelope encryption patterns. we can integrate with customer-managed KMS for key wrapping on private and dedicated private offerings. hosted can support BYOK but there's an extra attestation/connection step and limited vaulting windows.
02:12 Priya: Is that attestation something you can include in a contract? we need proof keys are not exported.
02:18 Maya: yes we can include contractual language and we have a tech attestation flow; we'll send the legal wording and the SOC2 artifact.
02:27 Daniel: About SSO — we use Okta and SAML 2.0. we need user-level RBAC mapped to our groups, and SAML assertion needs to carry role claim. do you surface RBAC at token or at service layer?
02:40 Liam: we map SAML group claims to RBAC roles in Redwood Console. there's also API-level scoped tokens you can mint per service account. small caveat: if you're on hosted and want fine-grained internal permissions, we recommend provisioning a dedicated customer org and using SAML + SCIM for group sync.
03:03 Hannah: SCIM is good. we have SCIM provisioning. any gotchas with SCIM mapping?
03:08 Jamal: sometimes attribute mappings need normalization. we usually provide a mapping doc and a test harness. for bigger orgs we do a one-off mapping run.
03:18 Priya: audit logs — how long do you retain them and can we push logs to our SIEM? chain of custody is important.
03:26 Liam: by default we retain audit logs 90 days in hosted. we can export logs to customer S3 or push syslog/forwarder into Splunk/Datadog. for Dedicated/Private we can increase retention and we support immutable log buckets for X days per contract.
03:44 Daniel: are there any PII redaction features or we are expected to filter upstream?
03:50 Jamal: we offer redaction tooling and prefix filters; but generally we recommend filtering PII before hitting the model for PHI workloads. for regulated workloads customers often choose Private deployment to keep data ingress controlled.
04:05 Priya: okay noted. regulatory wise do you have ISO 27001 and SOC2 type II reports available?
04:12 Maya: yes SOC2 Type II report available under NDA and ISO 27001 certificate — we will share summary docs and what audit scopes cover.
04:20 Priya: what about encryption in transit and at rest? specifics — TLS versions, key rotation cadence, HSM-backed keys?
04:28 Liam: TLS 1.2+ supported (we encourage 1.3), keys at rest are AES-256. for BYOK we integrate with customer managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) and HSM-backed key stores for private deployments; rotation policies are configurable.
04:45 Hannah: question on model k-v cache — is cache persisted to disk and could that contain PHI? how is that encrypted?
04:52 Jamal: KV cache is ephemeral in RAM by default; for long‑running sessions we persist shards to encrypted disks with customer-controlled keys on Private deployments. on hosted, persisted artifacts encrypted with our keys unless BYOK is in place.
05:10 Daniel: about the hosting tradeoff — if we need guaranteed no multi-tenancy leakage, sounds like Private or Dedicated is required. can you quantify the perf/cost difference?
05:22 Liam: roughly — hosted is lowest TCO for small scale, but you trade off control. Dedicated gives single-tenant GPU pools and better predictable latency; Private gives maximum control but with more ops overhead. we'll follow up with concrete pricing examples based on your QPS numbers.
05:40 Priya: ok next — SAML mis‑claims sometimes happen, in the past we've seen assertion replay issues. do you do SAML assertion replay protection?
05:48 Liam: yes we validate assertion timestamps and nonce, and advise short-lived auth sessions with refresh tokens and session revocation hooks via SCIM deprovisioning.
05:58 Maya: any questions from product side — Omar?
06:02 Omar (Lucidity - Product): i'm curious about prompt storage — are prompts logged? and can we opt-out of prompt retention?
06:10 Jamal: prompts are logged for safety and quality by default. we do offer configurations to turn off retention or to redact prompt content at ingestion for private deployments. hosted retention can be adjusted contractually but log forwarding to your SIEM is the recommended pattern.
06:26 Hannah: do you support field-level encryption where we encrypt fields before sending?
06:31 Liam: yes, field-level or client-side encryption works fine; you just need to ensure the model can still receive necessary context, obviously encrypted tokens won't be interpretable by the model unless you handle decryption in a secure enclave. many customers do hybrid patterns.
06:46 Priya: auditability: if there's a security incident, do you support forensic snapshots or point-in-time replays of logs?
06:54 Jamal: we can provide immutable log exports and can preserve request traces. for private deployments you keep the logs; for hosted we can export the relevant slices under NDA and with a defined retention.
07:12 Daniel: are you seeing egress hotspots, like data leaving region? we need EU residency for some datasets.
07:20 Liam: we route regionally by policy; for hosted we have EU regions and you can pin workloads. for Private, you choose region or on-prem. routing policies can ensure no cross-region egress.
07:33 Priya: cookie cutter question — do you have dedicated pen test reports and vulnerability scan cadence?
07:38 Maya: yes annual external pentests and quarterly internal scans; we share summary reports under NDA.
07:45 Priya: good. any third-party sub processors?
07:50 Maya: we maintain a subprocessor list and will send it. we also provide a data processing addendum.
07:58 Daniel: okay, practicalities: if we start a pilot, say 3 weeks, what does the onboarding look like and what endpoints are we hitting?
08:06 Liam: onboarding for hosted is an API key, quickstart prompts, and a small test harness. for dedicated/pilot we provision capacity and provide a VPC peering or private link and a customer organization in the console; there is a short network setup and KMS handshake. typical pilot 2–4 weeks.
08:28 Hannah: network wise do you support Private Link vs VPC peering?
08:32 Jamal: both, plus direct connect options for on-prem. Private Link is commonly used for minimal ingress egress exposure.
08:40 Priya: retention policy: we need 7 years for some records in case of litigation. do you support long-term storage of logs offline?
08:48 Liam: yes we can export logs to your S3 and maintain immutable retention buckets; that is normally part of an enterprise contract.
08:56 Maya: quick note on RBAC mapping — we can map Okta group claims to specific roles such as "prompt-runner", "model-admin", "audit-reader". we recommend least privilege by default.
09:12 Daniel: do you support fine-grained API tokens per microservice? we have many microservices that call the API.
09:17 Liam: yes service accounts and scoped tokens are supported; tokens can be issued via the console and rotated programmatically.
09:25 Hannah: any SLA on token rotation or compromise detection?
09:29 Jamal: we provide token rotation APIs and can integrate with your ops—compromise detection triggers session revocation.
09:36 Priya: curious about cost controls — can you limit max tokens per request or per user to reduce runaway bills?
09:41 Maya: yep quota controls, per-token spend alerts and rate limits are standard. we can create per-org quotas and per-token caps.
09:50 Omar: are there mechanisms for evals and quality regressions monitoring? we need to ensure quantization or q int8 doesn't regress outputs for clinical prompts.
09:59 Liam: Redwood Optimize monitors quality and can flag regression alerts; for dedicated/private you control quantization profiles but we recommend A/B testing before rollout.
10:10 Priya: any known limitations around FedRAMP or similar high-assurance compliance?
10:15 Maya: we do not have FedRAMP currently; for federal workloads we'd discuss private on-prem with specific accreditation efforts.
10:23 Daniel: ok — slightly practical: if we want to BYOK with AWS KMS, what's the sync flow? key wrapping only?
10:29 Jamal: typical flow: you create the customer key in AWS KMS, we request a grant with restricted operations, and we use envelope encryption; the master key never leaves your KMS. for Private deployments you retain full control.
10:42 Hannah: what about logs containing sensitive tokens accidentally, is there scrubbers or redactors?
10:47 Liam: we provide redaction pipelines and regex-based scrubbers and can do custom scrubbers as part of the pilot. we also advise client-side scrubbing.
10:56 Priya: if we go hosted but require BYOK, you said there's an attestation window. can you explain that?
11:02 Maya: sure — hosted BYOK requires a short-lived secure connection to the customer's KMS for key operations. we document the handshake and provide cryptographic proofs and audit logs for the key operations.
11:20 Daniel: any latency impact for KMS calls in-line? that's a big concern for UI latency.
11:27 Liam: we avoid synchronous KMS ops on the happy path; we use envelope encryption and local cache of data‑keys, with periodic rewraps to reduce latency. for super low latency, Private with local HSM is best.
11:45 Hannah: do you have examples of Healthcare customers or references? any case studies?
11:49 Maya: yes we have anonymized case studies and a healthcare reference list — we'll share names under NDA.
11:56 Priya: ok let's surface blockers: primary blockers are (1) contractual BYOK guarantees, (2) audit log retention & immutability, (3) SSO + SCIM mapping must meet our identity lifecycle.
12:12 Maya: noted. we'll include contractual language and a security addendum in the packet.
12:18 Daniel: what about regional residency for EU data?
12:22 Liam: you can pin model hosting to eu-west region and ensure your workloads run there; for private we can work with on-prem or region-specific deployments.
12:33 Priya: any threats from model fine-tuning leakage if we train shared models?
12:38 Jamal: Redwood separates training from serving; by default we don't allow customer-provided data to leak into shared model blends unless explicitly consented for fine-tuning. we can provide isolation guarantees for dedicated/private.
12:55 Omar: curious about rate limiting and burst protection — if we have a burst, how do you handle it?
13:02 Liam: we support burst capacity in Dedicated, and we have throttling backpressure in hosted; we also offer pre-warmed pools for predictable peaks.
13:18 Priya: timeline recap — procurement in 6–8 weeks. what would you like from us to size pilot?
13:24 Maya: expected QPS, peak tokens, list of PHI data types, and which endpoints you want integrated (UI vs batch).
13:32 Daniel: we'll collate that.
13:35 Hannah: anything on monitoring and tracing request origins? we need request-level tracing with user id for audits.
13:41 Jamal: we emit request ids and will include user identifiers per policy; logs can be forwarded to your tracing pipeline.
13:50 Priya: on legal — will you sign a BAA?
13:53 Maya: we do sign BAAs for healthcare customers; legal team will follow up on timeline.
14:00 Daniel: good. i'd like a technical deep dive next with network diagrams. can we line up a SE session?
14:06 Maya: yes Liam and Jamal will run that — want week of 21st?
14:10 Daniel: that works.
14:12 Maya: quick recap of next steps...
14:15 Maya: (recap) we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and subprocessor list, draft architecture for private/KMS flow, pricing scenarios and pilot plan. Lucidity will share traffic profile and identity diagrams.
14:28 Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
14:31 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites.

End of transcript.

Identity lifecycle (Okta + SCIM) is a gating item; RBAC claims must be mappable to internal groups.
KMS BYOK is negotiable; Private gives strongest guarantees and local HSM option for lowest latency and full control.
